The nine entries go from 4,308 to 7,442 characters. Five are still over 600: P-46 (1,247), P-48 (1,241), P-43 (1,172), P-44 (958) and P-49 (759). P-43 is held for the curator's answers, so its "Why:" sentence and "cares that specialised code runs fast" keep their wording; only "He" became "The curator".

- **P-42:** "a callout that keeps `Object`" read as text that still binds, and the compiled path's departure was a bare row number. I wrote "records that the Working Draft said `Object`" and said what the compiled path refuses (a generic instantiated at a tuple). I kept "functions" as written, because the audit's question on it is still open.
- **P-43:** the reader could not see why the rule forces a flat tower, "catch-all" was undefined, and route C was only a handle. I defined the rule and showed why a nested tower breaks it (from the exclusion design brief). I said what route C is and pointed to P-95, which keeps it open. I added a state line: `Number` still keeps its `=`, a default waiting for review (review-queue item 22). The audit's two questions are restated for the curator.
- **P-44:** "the 2012 way", "generic child" and "the 2008 one" leaned on the conversation, and there was no reason. I named the case (`Integral[\I\]` under `AnyIntegral`) and the team's 2012 texts. I added the reason that the question he accepted gave (P-26), and said that row 487's hole stays open under this decision. Added "Built."
- **P-46:** the example read as contradicting the title, and "answer 8's promotion" is a handle. I restored the decision's own clause, "a generic declaration applies if some type within its bounds takes the arguments" (here `T = Number`), and spelled out P-74's rule. I gave row 537 a few words, as a "Still to build:" line.
- **P-47:** "the family answers at the promoted type" was hard to parse. I replaced it with the decision's own case: an inherited `MAX` would tie with `QQ`'s, while each type's own declaration lets `b MAX 1` answer as `b + 1` does. The precedents became the reason he accepted ("the library's own device"). Added "Built."
- **P-48:** "do not fix" could be read two ways, and "still" made walk's use of the value's type look like a gap to close. I added the three cases from the question he answered, "`Any` if it has none", the three unbounded declarations by name, and "always" (his option's own word). Row 538 got a few words.
- **P-49:** "the context" and "the expected type" were two words for one thing, and "converts" and "only then" left doors open. I defined the expected type and used only that term, wrote "by coercion if need be" and "only when it keeps none", and added his reason. I added a state line: the checker as built makes one more attempt between the two, a default waiting for review (review-queue item 2). Row 508 (fixed) moved to the note line.
- **P-52:** the scope was implicit and "corner by corner" was not explained. The title now names `narrowToRange`, and the entry says which corners `PCMP` compares, axis by axis, and why the example raises. Added "Built." Row 657 (fixed) moved to the note line.
- **P-53:** mostly clear already. The reason (the declared `Maybe[\Char\]`) went into the title, and I added the question's own walk example, `Just(a)` for `"abc".left`. Added "Built." Row 606 (fixed) moved to the note line.

Added content to check:
- **"Built." lines:** the "Built." lines on P-44, P-47, P-52 and P-53 are added content. The record had dropped such lines on 10-13 as belonging to FACTS. The pilot's entries carry them, so I followed the pilot, and each one is backed by the audit's scout report.
- **Reasons:** the new "Why:" lines on P-44 and P-49 come from the question he accepted or from his own words.
- **Where to look:** each addition is flagged in that entry's "Meaning" section in `proposals.md`.
